What, is there none of Pygmalion's images, newly made woman, to be had now, for putting the hand in the pocket and extracting it clutch'd? What reply, ha? What sayest thou to this tune, matter and method? Is't not drowned i' the last rain, ha? What sayest thou, Trot? Is the world as it was, man? Which is the way? Is it sad, and few words? or how? The trick of it?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Still thus, and thus; still worse!
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: How doth my dear morsel, thy mistress? Procures she still, ha?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Why, 'tis good; it is the right of it; it must be so: ever your fresh whore and your powdered bawd: an unshunned consequence; it must be so. Art going to prison, Pompey?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Why, 'tis not amiss, Pompey. Farewell: go, say I sent thee thither. For debt, Pompey? or how?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Well, then, imprison him: if imprisonment be the due of a bawd, why, 'tis his right: bawd is he doubtless, and of antiquity too; bawd-born. Farewell, good Pompey. Commend me to the prison, Pompey: you will turn good husband now, Pompey; you will keep the house.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: No, indeed, will I not, Pompey; it is not the wear. I will pray, Pompey, to increase your bondage: If you take it not patiently, why, your mettle is the more. Adieu, trusty Pompey. 'Bless you, friar.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Does Bridget paint still, Pompey, ha?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Then, Pompey, nor now. What news abroad, friar? what news?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Go to kennel, Pompey; go. What news, friar, of the duke?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: I know none. Can you tell me of any?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Some say he is with the Emperor of Russia; other some, he is in Rome: but where is he, think you?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: I know not where; but wheresoever, I wish him well.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: It was a mad fantastical trick of him to steal from the state, and usurp the beggary he was never born to. Lord Angelo dukes it well in his absence; he puts transgression to 't.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: He does well in 't.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: A little more lenity to lechery would do no harm in him: something too crabbed that way, friar.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: It is too general a vice, and severity must cure it.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Yes, in good sooth, the vice is of a great kindred; it is well allied: but it is impossible to extirp it quite, friar, till eating and drinking be put down. They say this Angelo was not made by man and woman after this downright way of creation: is it true, think you?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: How should he be made, then?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Some report a sea-maid spawned him; some, that he was begot between two stock-fishes. But it is certain that when he makes water his urine is congealed ice; that I know to be true: and he is a motion generative; that's infallible.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: You are pleasant, sir, and speak apace.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Why, what a ruthless thing is this in him, for the rebellion of a codpiece to take away the life of a man! Would the duke that is absent have done this? Ere he would have hanged a man for the getting a hundred bastards, he would have paid for the nursing a thousand: he had some feeling of the sport: he knew the service, and that instructed him to mercy.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: I never heard the absent duke much detected for women; he was not inclined that way.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, sir, you are deceived.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Who, not the duke? yes, your beggar of fifty; and his use was to put a ducat in her clack-dish: the duke had crotchets in him. He would be drunk too; that let me inform you.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: You do him wrong, surely.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Sir, I was an inward of his. A shy fellow was the duke: and I believe I know the cause of his withdrawing.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: What, I prithee, might be the cause?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: No, pardon; 'tis a secret must be locked within the teeth and the lips: but this I can let you understand, the greater file of the subject held the duke to be wise.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Wise! why, no question but he was.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: A very superficial, ignorant, unweighing fellow.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Either this is the envy in you, folly, or mistaking: the very stream of his life and the business he hath helmed must upon a warranted need give him a better proclamation. Let him be but testimonied in his own bringings-forth, and he shall appear to the envious a scholar, a statesman and a soldier. Therefore you speak unskilfully: or if your knowledge be more it is much darkened in your malice.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Sir, I know him, and I love him.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Love talks with better knowledge, and knowledge with dearer love.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Come, sir, I know what I know.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: I can hardly believe that, since you know not what you speak. But, if ever the duke return, as our prayers are he may, let me desire you to make your answer before him. If it be honest you have spoke, you have courage to maintain it: I am bound to call upon you; and, I pray you, your name?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Sir, my name is Lucio; well known to the duke.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: He shall know you better, sir, if I may live to report you.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, you hope the duke will return no more; or you imagine me too unhurtful an opposite. But indeed I can do you little harm; you'll forswear this again.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I'll be hanged first: thou art deceived in me, friar. But no more of this. Canst thou tell if Claudio die to-morrow or no?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Why should he die, sir?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Why? For filling a bottle with a tundish. I would the duke we talk of were returned again: the ungenitured agent will unpeople the province with continency; sparrows must not build in his house-eaves, because they are lecherous. The duke yet would have dark deeds darkly answered; he would never bring them to light: would he were returned! Marry, this Claudio is condemned for untrussing. Farewell, good friar: I prithee, pray for me. The duke, I say to thee again, would eat mutton on Fridays. He's not past it yet, and I say to thee, he would mouth with a beggar, though she smelt brown bread and garlic: say that I said so. Farewell.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: No might nor greatness in mortality Can censure 'scape; back-wounding calumny The whitest virtue strikes. What king so strong Can tie the gall up in the slanderous tongue? But who comes here?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Bliss and goodness on you!
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Not of this country, though my chance is now To use it for my time: I am a brother Of gracious order, late come from the See In special business from his holiness.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: None, but that there is so great a fever on goodness, that the dissolution of it must cure it: novelty is only in request; and it is as dangerous to be aged in any kind of course, as it is virtuous to be constant in any undertaking. There is scarce truth enough alive to make societies secure; but security enough to make fellowships accurst: much upon this riddle runs the wisdom of the world. This news is old enough, yet it is every day's news. I pray you, sir, of what disposition was the duke?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: What pleasure was he given to?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: He professes to have received no sinister measure from his judge, but most willingly humbles himself to the determination of justice: yet had he framed to himself, by the instruction of his frailty, many deceiving promises of life; which I by my good leisure have discredited to him, and now is he resolved to die.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: If his own life answer the straitness of his proceeding, it shall become him well; wherein if he chance to fail, he hath sentenced himself.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Peace be with you! He who the sword of heaven will bear Should be as holy as severe; Pattern in himself to know, Grace to stand, and virtue go; More nor less to others paying Than by self-offences weighing. Shame to him whose cruel striking Kills for faults of his own liking! Twice treble shame on Angelo, To weed my vice and let his grow! O, what may man within him hide, Though angel on the outward side! How may likeness made in crimes, Making practise on the times, To draw with idle spiders' strings Most ponderous and substantial things!
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: 'Tis good; though music oft hath such a charm To make bad good, and good provoke to harm. I pray, you, tell me, hath any body inquired for me here to-day? much upon this time have I promised here to meet.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I do constantly believe you. The time is come even now. I shall crave your forbearance a little: may be I will call upon you anon, for some advantage to yourself.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Very well met, and well come. What is the news from this good deputy?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: He hath a garden circummured with brick, Whose western side is with a vineyard back'd; And to that vineyard is a planched gate,
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: But shall you on your knowledge find this way?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Are there no other tokens Between you 'greed concerning her observance?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: No, none, but only a repair i' the dark; And that I have possess'd him my most stay Can be but brief; for I have made him know I have a servant comes with me along, That stays upon me, whose persuasion is I come about my brother.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: 'Tis well borne up. I have not yet made known to Mariana A word of this. What, ho! within! come forth! I pray you, be acquainted with this maid; She comes to do you good.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I do desire the like.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Do you persuade yourself that I respect you?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Take, then, this your companion by the hand, Who hath a story ready for your ear. I shall attend your leisure: but make haste; The vaporous night approaches.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O place and greatness! millions of false eyes Are stuck upon thee: volumes of report Run with these false and most contrarious quests Upon thy doings: thousand escapes of wit Make thee the father of their idle dreams And rack thee in their fancies. Welcome, how agreed?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: She'll take the enterprise upon her, father, If you advise it.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: It is not my consent, But my entreaty too.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Little have you to say When you depart from him, but, soft and low, 'Remember now my brother.'
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Nor, gentle daughter, fear you not at all. He is your husband on a pre-contract: To bring you thus together, 'tis no sin, Sith that the justice of your title to him Doth flourish the deceit. Come, let us go: Our corn's to reap, for yet our tithe's to sow.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: The best and wholesomest spirts of the night Envelope you, good Provost! Who call'd here of late?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: They will, then, ere't be long.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Not so, not so; his life is parallel'd
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Have you no countermand for Claudio yet, But he must die to-morrow?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: As near the dawning, provost, as it is, You shall hear more ere morning.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: And here comes Claudio's pardon.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: What is that Barnardine who is to be executed in the afternoon?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: How came it that the absent duke had not either delivered him to his liberty or executed him? I have heard it was ever his manner to do so.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Hath he born himself penitently in prison? how seems he to be touched?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: More of him anon. There is written in your brow, provost, honesty and constancy: if I read it not truly, my ancient skill beguiles me; but, in the boldness of my cunning, I will lay myself in hazard. Claudio, whom here you have warrant to execute, is no greater forfeit to the law than Angelo who hath sentenced him. To make you understand this in a manifested effect, I crave but four days' respite; for the which you are to do me both a present and a dangerous courtesy.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: By the vow of mine order I warrant you, if my instructions may be your guide. Let this Barnardine be this morning executed, and his head born to Angelo.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, death's a great disguiser; and you may add to it. Shave the head, and tie the beard; and say it was the desire of the penitent to be so bared before his death: you know the course is common. If any thing fall to you upon this, more than thanks and good fortune, by the saint whom I profess, I will plead against it with my life.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Were you sworn to the duke, or to the deputy?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: You will think you have made no offence, if the duke avouch the justice of your dealing?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Not a resemblance, but a certainty. Yet since I see you fearful, that neither my coat, integrity, nor persuasion can with ease attempt you, I will go further than I meant, to pluck all fears out of you. Look you, sir, here is the hand and seal of the duke: you know the character, I doubt not; and the signet is not strange to you.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: The contents of this is the return of the duke: you shall anon over-read it at your pleasure; where you shall find, within these two days he will be here. This is a thing that Angelo knows not; for he this very day receives letters of strange tenor; perchance of the duke's death; perchance entering into some monastery; but, by chance, nothing of what is writ. Look, the unfolding star calls up the shepherd. Put not yourself into amazement how these things should be: all difficulties are but easy when they are known. Call your executioner, and off with Barnardine's head: I will give him a present shrift and advise him for a better place. Yet you are amazed; but this shall absolutely resolve you. Come away; it is almost clear dawn.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Sir, induced by my charity, and hearing how hastily you are to depart, I am come to advise you, comfort you and pray with you.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, sir, you must: and therefore I beseech you Look forward on the journey you shall go.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Unfit to live or die: O gravel heart! After him, fellows; bring him to the block.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: A creature unprepared, unmeet for death; And to transport him in the mind he is Were damnable.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, 'tis an accident that heaven provides! Dispatch it presently; the hour draws on Prefix'd by Angelo: see this be done, And sent according to command; whiles I Persuade this rude wretch willingly to die.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Let this be done. Put them in secret holds, both Barnardine and Claudio: Ere twice the sun hath made his journal greeting To the under generation, you shall find Your safety manifested.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Quick, dispatch, and send the head to Angelo. Now will I write letters to Angelo,-- The provost, he shall bear them, whose contents Shall witness to him I am near at home, And that, by great injunctions, I am bound To enter publicly: him I'll desire To meet me at the consecrated fount A league below the city; and from thence, By cold gradation and well-balanced form, We shall proceed with Angelo.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Convenient is it. Make a swift return; For I would commune with you of such things That want no ear but yours.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: The tongue of Isabel. She's come to know
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Good morning to you, fair and gracious daughter.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: The better, given me by so holy a man. Hath yet the deputy sent my brother's pardon?
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: He hath released him, Isabel, from the world: His head is off and sent to Angelo.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Nay, but it is not so.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: It is no other: show your wisdom, daughter, In your close patience.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, I will to him and pluck out his eyes!
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: You shall not be admitted to his sight.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Unhappy Claudio! wretched Isabel! Injurious world! most damned Angelo!
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: This nor hurts him nor profits you a jot; Forbear it therefore; give your cause to heaven. Mark what I say, which you shall find
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I am directed by you.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: This letter, then, to Friar Peter give;
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Good even. Friar, where's the provost?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: O pretty Isabella, I am pale at mine heart to see thine eyes so red: thou must be patient. I am fain to dine and sup with water and bran; I dare not for my head fill my belly; one fruitful meal would set me to 't. But they say the duke will be here to-morrow. By my troth, Isabel, I loved thy brother: if the old fantastical duke of dark corners had been at home, he had lived.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Sir, the duke is marvellous little beholding to your reports; but the best is, he lives not in them.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Friar, thou knowest not the duke so well as I do: he's a better woodman than thou takest him for.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Well, you'll answer this one day. Fare ye well.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Nay, tarry; I'll go along with thee I can tell thee pretty tales of the duke.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: You have told me too many of him already, sir, if they be true; if not true, none were enough.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I was once before him for getting a wench with child.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Did you such a thing?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Yes, marry, did I but I was fain to forswear it; they would else have married me to the rotten medlar.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Sir, your company is fairer than honest. Rest you well.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: By my troth, I'll go with thee to the lane's end: if bawdy talk offend you, we'll have very little of it. Nay, friar, I am a kind of burr; I shall stick.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: These letters at fit time deliver me The provost knows our purpose and our plot. The matter being afoot, keep your instruction, And hold you ever to our special drift; Though sometimes you do blench from this to that, As cause doth minister. Go call at Flavius' house, And tell him where I stay: give the like notice To Valentinus, Rowland, and to Crassus, And bid them bring the trumpets to the gate; But send me Flavius first.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I thank thee, Varrius; thou hast made good haste: Come, we will walk. There's other of our friends Will greet us here anon, my gentle Varrius.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Besides, he tells me that, if peradventure He speak against me on the adverse side, I should not think it strange; for 'tis a physic That's bitter to sweet end.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: O, peace! the friar is come.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: My very worthy cousin, fairly met! Our old and faithful friend, we are glad to see you.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Many and hearty thankings to you both. We have made inquiry of you; and we hear Such goodness of your justice, that our soul Cannot but yield you forth to public thanks, Forerunning more requital.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, your desert speaks loud; and I should wrong it, To lock it in the wards of covert bosom, When it deserves, with characters of brass, A forted residence 'gainst the tooth of time And razure of oblivion. Give me your hand, And let the subject see, to make them know That outward courtesies would fain proclaim Favours that keep within. Come, Escalus, You must walk by us on our other hand; And good supporters are you.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Justice, O royal duke! Vail your regard Upon a wrong'd, I would fain have said, a maid! O worthy prince, dishonour not your eye By throwing it on any other object Till you have heard me in my true complaint And given me justice, justice, justice, justice!
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Relate your wrongs; in what? by whom? be brief.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Most strange, but yet most truly, will I speak: That Angelo's forsworn; is it not strange? That Angelo's a murderer; is 't not strange? That Angelo is an adulterous thief, An hypocrite, a virgin-violator; Is it not strange and strange?
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Nay, it is ten times strange.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: It is not truer he is Angelo
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Away with her! Poor soul, She speaks this in the infirmity of sense.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O prince, I conjure thee, as thou believest There is another comfort than this world, That thou neglect me not, with that opinion That I am touch'd with madness! Make not impossible That which but seems unlike: 'tis not impossible But one, the wicked'st caitiff on the ground, May seem as shy, as grave, as just, as absolute As Angelo; even so may Angelo, In all his dressings, characts, titles, forms, Be an arch-villain; believe it, royal prince: If he be less, he's nothing; but he's more, Had I more name for badness.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: By mine honesty, If she be mad,--as I believe no other,-- Her madness hath the oddest frame of sense, Such a dependency of thing on thing, As e'er I heard in madness.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O gracious duke, Harp not on that, nor do not banish reason For inequality; but let your reason serve To make the truth appear where it seems hid, And hide the false seems true.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Many that are not mad Have, sure, more lack of reason. What would you say?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I am the sister of one Claudio, Condemn'd upon the act of fornication To lose his head; condemn'd by Angelo: I, in probation of a sisterhood, Was sent to by my brother; one Lucio As then the messenger,--
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: That's I, an't like your grace: I came to her from Claudio, and desired her To try her gracious fortune with Lord Angelo For her poor brother's pardon.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: You were not bid to speak.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: No, my good lord; Nor wish'd to hold my peace.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: I wish you now, then; Pray you, take note of it: and when you have A business for yourself, pray heaven you then Be perfect.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: The warrants for yourself; take heed to't.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: This gentleman told somewhat of my tale,--
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: It may be right; but you are i' the wrong To speak before your time. Proceed.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I went To this pernicious caitiff deputy,--
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Pardon it; The phrase is to the matter.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Mended again. The matter; proceed.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: In brief, to set the needless process by, How I persuaded, how I pray'd, and kneel'd, How he refell'd me, and how I replied,-- For this was of much length,--the vile conclusion
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: O, that it were as like as it is true!
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: By heaven, fond wretch, thou knowist not what thou speak'st, Or else thou art suborn'd against his honour In hateful practise. First, his integrity Stands without blemish. Next, it imports no reason That with such vehemency he should pursue Faults proper to himself: if he had so offended, He would have weigh'd thy brother by himself And not have cut him off. Some one hath set you on: Confess the truth, and say by whose advice Thou camest here to complain.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: And is this all? Then, O you blessed ministers above, Keep me in patience, and with ripen'd time Unfold the evil which is here wrapt up In countenance! Heaven shield your grace from woe, As I, thus wrong'd, hence unbelieved go!
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: I know you'ld fain be gone. An officer! To prison with her! Shall we thus permit A blasting and a scandalous breath to fall On him so near us? This needs must be a practise. Who knew of Your intent and coming hither?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: One that I would were here, Friar Lodowick.
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: A ghostly father, belike. Who knows that Lodowick?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: My lord, I know him; 'tis a meddling friar; I do not like the man: had he been lay, my lord For certain words he spake against your grace In your retirement, I had swinged him soundly.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Words against me? this is a good friar, belike! And to set on this wretched woman here Against our substitute! Let this friar be found.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: But yesternight, my lord, she and that friar, I saw them at the prison: a saucy friar, A very scurvy fellow.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: We did believe no less. Know you that Friar Lodowick that she speaks of?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: My lord, most villanously; believe it.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Good friar, let's hear it. Do you not smile at this, Lord Angelo? O heaven, the vanity of wretched fools! Give us some seats. Come, cousin Angelo; In this I'll be impartial; be you judge Of your own cause. Is this the witness, friar? First, let her show her face, and after speak.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Why, you are nothing then: neither maid, widow, nor wife?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: My lord, she may be a punk; for many of them are neither maid, widow, nor wife.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Silence that fellow: I would he had some cause To prattle for himself.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: He was drunk then, my lord: it can be no better.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: For the benefit of silence, would thou wert so too!
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: This is no witness for Lord Angelo.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: No? you say your husband.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Ay, with my heart And punish them to your height of pleasure. Thou foolish friar, and thou pernicious woman, Compact with her that's gone, think'st thou thy oaths, Though they would swear down each particular saint, Were testimonies against his worth and credit That's seal'd in approbation? You, Lord Escalus, Sit with my cousin; lend him your kind pains To find out this abuse, whence 'tis derived. There is another friar that set them on; Let him be sent for.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Go do it instantly. And you, my noble and well-warranted cousin, Whom it concerns to hear this matter forth, Do with your injuries as seems you best, In any chastisement: I for a while will leave you; But stir not you till you have well determined Upon these slanderers.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: 'Cucullus non facit monachum:' honest in nothing but in his clothes; and one that hath spoke most villanous speeches of the duke.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: As any in Vienna, on my word.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Not better than he, by her own report.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Marry, sir, I think, if you handled her privately, she would sooner confess: perchance, publicly, she'll be ashamed.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: That's the way; for women are light at midnight.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: My lord, here comes the rascal I spoke of; here with the provost.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Respect to your great place! and let the devil Be sometime honour'd for his burning throne! Where is the duke? 'tis he should hear me speak.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Boldly, at least. But, O, poor souls, Come you to seek the lamb here of the fox? Good night to your redress! Is the duke gone? Then is your cause gone too. The duke's unjust, Thus to retort your manifest appeal, And put your trial in the villain's mouth Which here you come to accuse.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: This is the rascal; this is he I spoke of.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Be not so hot; the duke Dare no more stretch this finger of mine than he Dare rack his own: his subject am I not, Nor here provincial. My business in this state Made me a looker on here in Vienna, Where I have seen corruption boil and bubble Till it o'er-run the stew; laws for all faults, But faults so countenanced, that the strong statutes Stand like the forfeits in a barber's shop, As much in mock as mark.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: 'Tis he, my lord. Come hither, goodman baldpate: do you know me?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: I remember you, sir, by the sound of your voice: I met you at the prison, in the absence of the duke.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, did you so? And do you remember what you said of the duke?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Do you so, sir? And was the duke a fleshmonger, a fool, and a coward, as you then reported him to be?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: You must, sir, change persons with me, ere you make that my report: you, indeed, spoke so of him; and much more, much worse.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O thou damnable fellow! Did not I pluck thee by the nose for thy speeches?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: I protest I love the duke as I love myself.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Come, sir; come, sir; come, sir; foh, sir! Why, you bald-pated, lying rascal, you must be hooded, must you? Show your knave's visage, with a pox to you! show your sheep-biting face, and be hanged an hour! Will't not off?
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Thou art the first knave that e'er madest a duke. First, provost, let me bail these gentle three. Sneak not away, sir; for the friar and you Must have a word anon. Lay hold on him.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: This may prove worse than hanging.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Come hither, Mariana. Say, wast thou e'er contracted to this woman?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Go take her hence, and marry her instantly. Do you the office, friar; which consummate, Return him here again. Go with him, provost.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Come hither, Isabel. Your friar is now your prince: as I was then Advertising and holy to your business, Not changing heart with habit, I am still Attorney'd at your service.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: O, give me pardon, That I, your vassal, have employ'd and pain'd Your unknown sovereignty!
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: You are pardon'd, Isabel: And now, dear maid, be you as free to us. Your brother's death, I know, sits at your heart; And you may marvel why I obscured myself, Labouring to save his life, and would not rather Make rash remonstrance of my hidden power Than let him so be lost. O most kind maid, It was the swift celerity of his death, Which I did think with slower foot came on, That brain'd my purpose. But, peace be with him! That life is better life, past fearing death, Than that which lives to fear: make it your comfort, So happy is your brother.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: For this new-married man approaching here, Whose salt imagination yet hath wrong'd Your well defended honour, you must pardon For Mariana's sake: but as he adjudged your brother,-- Being criminal, in double violation Of sacred chastity and of promise-breach Thereon dependent, for your brother's life,-- The very mercy of the law cries out Most audible, even from his proper tongue, 'An Angelo for Claudio, death for death!' Haste still pays haste, and leisure answers leisure; Like doth quit like, and MEASURE still FOR MEASURE. Then, Angelo, thy fault's thus manifested; Which, though thou wouldst deny, denies thee vantage. We do condemn thee to the very block Where Claudio stoop'd to death, and with like haste. Away with him!
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: It is your husband mock'd you with a husband. Consenting to the safeguard of your honour, I thought your marriage fit; else imputation, For that he knew you, might reproach your life And choke your good to come; for his possessions, Although by confiscation they are ours, We do instate and widow you withal, To buy you a better husband.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Never crave him; we are definitive.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: You do but lose your labour. Away with him to death! Now, sir, to you.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: He dies for Claudio's death.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Most bounteous sir, Look, if it please you, on this man condemn'd, As if my brother lived: I partly think A due sincerity govern'd his deeds, Till he did look on me: since it is so, Let him not die. My brother had but justice,
Speaker: ISABELLA

Text: Your suit's unprofitable; stand up, I say. I have bethought me of another fault. Provost, how came it Claudio was beheaded At an unusual hour?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Had you a special warrant for the deed?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I would thou hadst done so by Claudio. Go fetch him hither; let me look upon him.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: There was a friar told me of this man. Sirrah, thou art said to have a stubborn soul. That apprehends no further than this world, And squarest thy life according. Thou'rt condemn'd: But, for those earthly faults, I quit them all; And pray thee take this mercy to provide For better times to come. Friar, advise him; I leave him to your hand. What muffled fellow's that?
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: 'Faith, my lord. I spoke it but according to the trick. If you will hang me for it, you may; but I had rather it would please you I might be whipt.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Whipt first, sir, and hanged after. Proclaim it, provost, round about the city. Is any woman wrong'd by this lewd fellow, As I have heard him swear himself there's one Whom he begot with child, let her appear, And he shall marry her: the nuptial finish'd, Let him be whipt and hang'd.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: I beseech your highness, do not marry me to a whore. Your highness said even now, I made you a duke: good my lord, do not recompense me in making me a cuckold.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Upon mine honour, thou shalt marry her. Thy slanders I forgive; and therewithal Remit thy other forfeits. Take him to prison; And see our pleasure herein executed.
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Marrying a punk, my lord, is pressing to death, whipping, and hanging.
Speaker: LUCIO

Text: Slandering a prince deserves it. She, Claudio, that you wrong'd, look you restore. Joy to you, Mariana! Love her, Angelo: I have confess'd her and I know her virtue. Thanks, good friend Escalus, for thy much goodness: There's more behind that is more gratulate. Thanks, provost, for thy care and secrecy: We shill employ thee in a worthier place. Forgive him, Angelo, that brought you home
Speaker: DUKE VINCENTIO

Text: Mi perdonato, gentle master mine, I am in all affected as yourself; Glad that you thus continue your resolve To suck the sweets of sweet philosophy. Only, good master, while we do admire This virtue and this moral discipline, Let's be no stoics nor no stocks, I pray; Or so devote to Aristotle's cheques
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Master, some show to welcome us to town.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Hush, master! here's some good pastime toward: That wench is stark mad or wonderful froward.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Well said, master; mum! and gaze your fill.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: I pray, sir, tell me, is it possible That love should of a sudden take such hold?
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Master, it is no time to chide you now;
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Master, you look'd so longly on the maid, Perhaps you mark'd not what's the pith of all.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Saw you no more? mark'd you not how her sister Began to scold and raise up such a storm That mortal ears might hardly endure the din?
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Nay, then, 'tis time to stir him from his trance. I pray, awake, sir: if you love the maid, Bend thoughts and wits to achieve her. Thus it stands: Her eldest sister is so curst and shrewd That till the father rid his hands of her, Master, your love must live a maid at home; And therefore has he closely mew'd her up, Because she will not be annoy'd with suitors.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Ay, marry, am I, sir; and now 'tis plotted.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Master, for my hand, Both our inventions meet and jump in one.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Not possible; for who shall bear your part, And be in Padua here Vincentio's son, Keep house and ply his book, welcome his friends, Visit his countrymen and banquet them?
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: So had you need. In brief, sir, sith it your pleasure is, And I am tied to be obedient; For so your father charged me at our parting, 'Be serviceable to my son,' quoth he, Although I think 'twas in another sense; I am content to be Lucentio, Because so well I love Lucentio.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: So could I, faith, boy, to have the next wish after, That Lucentio indeed had Baptista's youngest daughter. But, sirrah, not for my sake, but your master's, I advise
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: Verona, for a while I take my leave, To see my friends in Padua, but of all My best beloved and approved friend, Hortensio; and I trow this is his house. Here, sirrah Grumio; knock, I say.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Villain, I say, knock me here soundly.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Villain, I say, knock me at this gate And rap me well, or I'll knock your knave's pate.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Will it not be? Faith, sirrah, an you'll not knock, I'll ring it; I'll try how you can sol, fa, and sing it.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Now, knock when I bid you, sirrah villain!
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Signior Hortensio, come you to part the fray? 'Con tutto il cuore, ben trovato,' may I say.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: A senseless villain! Good Hortensio, I bade the rascal knock upon your gate And could not get him for my heart to do it.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Sirrah, be gone, or talk not, I advise you.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Such wind as scatters young men through the world, To seek their fortunes farther than at home Where small experience grows. But in a few, Signior Hortensio, thus it stands with me: Antonio, my father, is deceased; And I have thrust myself into this maze,
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Signior Hortensio, 'twixt such friends as we Few words suffice; and therefore, if thou know One rich enough to be Petruchio's wife, As wealth is burden of my wooing dance, Be she as foul as was Florentius' love, As old as Sibyl and as curst and shrewd As Socrates' Xanthippe, or a worse, She moves me not, or not removes, at least, Affection's edge in me, were she as rough
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Hortensio, peace! thou know'st not gold's effect: Tell me her father's name and 'tis enough; For I will board her, though she chide as loud As thunder when the clouds in autumn crack.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: I know her father, though I know not her; And he knew my deceased father well. I will not sleep, Hortensio, till I see her; And therefore let me be thus bold with you To give you over at this first encounter, Unless you will accompany me thither.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Why came I hither but to that intent? Think you a little din can daunt mine ears? Have I not in my time heard lions roar? Have I not heard the sea puff'd up with winds Rage like an angry boar chafed with sweat? Have I not heard great ordnance in the field, And heaven's artillery thunder in the skies? Have I not in a pitched battle heard Loud 'larums, neighing steeds, and trumpets' clang? And do you tell me of a woman's tongue, That gives not half so great a blow to hear As will a chestnut in a farmer's fire? Tush, tush! fear boys with bugs.

Text: A good swift simile, but something currish.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: 'Tis well, sir, that you hunted for yourself: 'Tis thought your deer does hold you at a bay.
Speaker: TRANIO

Text: A' has a little gall'd me, I confess; And, as the jest did glance away from me, 'Tis ten to one it maim'd you two outright.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Well, I say no: and therefore for assurance Let's each one send unto his wife; And he whose wife is most obedient To come at first when he doth send for her, Shall win the wager which we will propose.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Twenty crowns! I'll venture so much of my hawk or hound, But twenty times so much upon my wife.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: How! she is busy and she cannot come! Is that an answer?
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: O, ho! entreat her! Nay, then she must needs come.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Worse and worse; she will not come! O vile, Intolerable, not to be endured! Sirrah Grumio, go to your mistress; Say, I command her to come to me.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: The fouler fortune mine, and there an end.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Where is your sister, and Hortensio's wife?
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Go fetch them hither: if they deny to come.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Marry, peace it bodes, and love and quiet life, And awful rule and right supremacy; And, to be short, what not, that's sweet and happy?
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Nay, I will win my wager better yet And show more sign of her obedience, Her new-built virtue and obedience. See where she comes and brings your froward wives As prisoners to her womanly persuasion. Katharina, that cap of yours becomes you not: Off with that bauble, throw it under-foot.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Katharina, I charge thee, tell these headstrong women What duty they do owe their lords and husbands.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Come on, I say; and first begin with her.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: I say she shall: and first begin with her.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Why, there's a wench! Come on, and kiss me, Kate.
Speaker: PETRUCHIO

Text: Come, Kate, we'll to bed. We three are married, but you two are sped. 'Twas I won the wager, though you hit the white; And, being a winner, God give you good night!
Speaker: PETRUCHIO
